title: Persistent JavaScript References
text: Use ctx$eval() source execute existing context return R value. Unlike qjs_eval(), preserves global state calls. Use ctx$compile() global script execute repeatedly. Compilation parses source without running . js_script_run() converts result R, js_script_run_ref() retains result JavaScript. Compiled scripts take arguments. parameterised repeated work, evaluate function eval_ref() invoke js_ref_call().
code: bare_ctx$eval("globalThis.count = 0; count") #> [1] 0 bare_ctx$eval("count += 1; count") #> [1] 1 increment <- bare_ctx$compile("count += 1; count") js_script_run(increment) #> [1] 2 js_script_run(increment) #> [1] 3  array_script <- bare_ctx$compile("[count, count + 1]") array_result <- js_script_run_ref(array_script) js_ref_to_r(array_result) #> [1] 3 4 double <- bare_ctx$eval_ref("value => value * 2") js_ref_to_r(js_ref_call(double, 21)) #> [1] 42

title: Working with R and JS Types
text: Use js_typed_array() raw, integer, double vector cross boundary contiguous typed storage rather ordinary JavaScript array. Raw vectors become Uint8Array, integer vectors become Int32Array, double vectors become Float64Array. Integer vectors containing NA rejected Int32Array missing-value representation. Double NA NaN values treated JavaScript NaN. return, Int32Array value -2147483648 becomes R’s NA_integer_ sentinel. JavaScript 64-bit BigInt arrays return doubles can lose precision outside exact integer range R double. JavaScript typed arrays copied directly matching R vector storage return. Use persistent reference value remain JavaScript across several operations, materialise R needs result.
code: ctx <- JSContext$new() ctx$source(code = paste(   "function typeName(x) { return x.constructor.name; }",   "function total(x) { return x.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0); }" ))  values <- js_typed_array(as.double(1:1000)) ctx$call("typeName", values) #> [1] "Float64Array" ctx$call("total", values) #> [1] 500500

title: Working with R and JS Types
text: Use js_masked_typed_array() logical, integer, double values need contiguous typed storage without losing R missing values. JavaScript receives branded object containing values, validity, length. Logical values use Uint8Array, integers use Int32Array, doubles use Float64Array. validity mask Uint8Array zero missing one valid. double NA masked, ordinary NaN remains valid Float64 value. JavaScript may modify buffers. Returning branded object reconstructs corresponding R vector using current contents. mask costs one byte per element, js_typed_array() remains preferable missing-value metadata unnecessary. Factors dates excluded class semantics require numeric storage validity mask.
code: ctx$source(code = paste(   "function fillMissing(x) {",   "  x.values[1] = 20;",   "  x.validity[1] = 1;",   "  return x;",   "}" ))  masked <- js_masked_typed_array(c(10L, NA_integer_, 30L)) ctx$call("fillMissing", masked) #> [1] 10 20 30

title: Working with R and JS Types
text: Use js_readonly_view() JavaScript needs read R vector. View creation wraps retains R vector copy convert elements. Conversion happens one element time JavaScript reads indexed values. Views array-like rather typed arrays. length, indexed access, iteration, inherited Array methods. view.toArray(), spread syntax, Array.(view) create ordinary mutable JavaScript array. Direct writes deletes throw error. JavaScript object retains wrapper vector full lifetime. Normal assignment R still follows copy--write rules: changing R binding can create new vector existing JavaScript view continues see retained vector. Passing view back R returns retained object directly. Use view JavaScript reads small part large vector avoiding initial transfer important. Use js_typed_array() JavaScript scan vector repeatedly, needs typed-array APIs, needs mutable independent copy.
code: ctx$source(code = paste(   "function endpoints(x) { return [x[0], x[x.length - 1]]; }",   "function viewTotal(x) { return x.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0); }" ))  view <- js_readonly_view(as.double(1:1000)) ctx$call("endpoints", view) #> [1]    1 1000 ctx$call("viewTotal", view) #> [1] 500500

title: Working with R and JS Types
text: Use js_mutable_view() JavaScript needs repeated, sparse mutation vector R needs observe changes without full return conversion. wrapper owns independent R copy, input binding never changed. Creating wrapper copies vector . Passing JavaScript constant time, indexed reads writes operate directly retained R storage. Returning JavaScript view recovers wrapper without materialising array. Mutable views fixed-length array-like objects rather typed arrays. Existing elements can replaced directly methods reverse(), sort(), fill(), copyWithin(). Adding properties, growing view, deleting elements throws error. Writes type checked, null undefined representing R missing values except raw vectors. unclassed raw, logical, integer, double, character vectors accepted. R modifies view$value JavaScript retains view, normal R copy--write can detach R binding retained storage. Complete R updates retaining mutable view, treat JavaScript writer. Use mutable view sparse repeated mutation shared R. Use js_typed_array() JavaScript needs typed-array APIs perform dense numeric work entirely inside JavaScript.

title: Expose an R vector as a read-only JavaScript view — js_readonly_view
text: view length, indexed access, array iteration, inherited non-mutating Array methods. Use view.toArray() Array.(view) mutable JavaScript array required. Attempts write delete indexed values throw error. wrapper copy vector. view retains wrapper vector JavaScript releases . Normal R assignment follows R's copy--write rules, modifying R binding can detach storage retained existing view. Returning view R recovers wrapper without materialising JavaScript array. Missing values use ordinary conversion rules: logical, integer, double, character NA become JavaScript null; NaN remains NaN. Factors yield labels, dates yield JavaScript dates.

title: Expose an R vector as a read-only JavaScript view — js_readonly_view
code: ctx <- JSContext$new(profile = "bare") ctx$source(code = paste(   "function endpoints(x) { return [x[0], x[x.length - 1]]; }",   "function total(x) { return x.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0); }" )) values <- js_readonly_view(as.double(1:1000)) ctx$call("endpoints", values) #> [1]    1 1000 ctx$call("total", values) #> [1] 500500

title: Create an R ALTREP view over a JavaScript typed array — js_ref_to_altrep
text: backing ArrayBuffer made permanently immutable address exposed R. affects every JavaScript alias buffer. Indexed JavaScript writes ignored, mutating typed-array methods, DataView writes, resizing, transfer operations throw error. ALTREP object retains reference context reads JavaScript buffer. R requests writable storage, values copied ordinary R vector, R modification affects copy, JavaScript reference can released. Shared, detached, unsupported, --bounds typed-array buffers rejected. Int32Array value -2147483648 R's NA_integer_ sentinel. Float64 NaN payloads preserved, including R NA_real_ payload originally transferred JavaScript. ALTREP-aware R operations can read buffer without copying. R code may request writable materialised storage therefore trigger copy.

title: Create an R ALTREP view over a JavaScript typed array — js_ref_to_altrep
code: ctx <- JSContext$new(profile = "bare") ref <- ctx$eval_ref("new Float64Array([1, 2, 3, 4])") values <- js_ref_to_altrep(ref) sum(values) #> [1] 10 values[1] #> [1] 1
